Article Title: Isro will never be privatised, its role won't be diminished: Space Agency & INSPACe chief
Article Text:
Isro dismisses privatisation speculation, says role will only strengthen

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most important focus for Isro in the future? Advanced R&D Human spaceflight Next-generation launch systems 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI/BENGALURU: Allaying the fears of some of its staff that the organisation will be privatised and its role reduced to an R&D lab, Isro Sunday dismissed “speculation” about any diminution of its role as “misinformation”.“These assertions are completely baseless and incorrect. We wish to categorically state that Isro will neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished,” it said.Isro further said it would continue to remain “India’s principal institution for advanced space research and technology development, national and strategic missions, space science and exploration, and critical and frontier space capabilities”.Space promoter and regulator Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (INSPACe) chairperson Pawan Goenka also said Sunday that Isro would “remain the bedrock of the Indian space sector” and at the core of India’s space programme leading frontier research and the next generation of national missions like the space station and Gaganyaan.The agency said, “Participation of private sector in space is not about reducing its role.It is about enabling Isro to focus even more strongly on the next generation of India’s space programme, while industry scales mature technologies and capabilities. What is changing is not the importance of Isro, but the scale and structure of India’s space ecosystem. The transition is therefore towards an Isro-led national space ecosystem. ”The agency also said its role would progressively strengthen in areas where “its scientific expertise matters most: frontier R&D, advanced technologies, human spaceflight, next-generation launch systems, deep-space and planetary missions and strategic national capabilities. It will continue developing cutting-edge technologies, including advanced payloads for communication, navigation and Earth observation, sensors, propulsion systems and other critical technologies”.After nine Isro staff associations representing thousands sought clarification from the agency chairperson on the private sector shift, Goenka said on X, “Let me say it unequivocally: Isro’s role is by no means diminishing.”On scaling up the production of rockets and satellites in India, the INSPACe director declared that the country had set an “ambitious target” of 50 launches a year by 2030. “A goal of this scale cannot be achieved by one organisation alone. Govt and private industry have to build this future together,” he said.The INSPACe chairperson said, “The reforms since 2020 are about expanding India’s overall space ecosystem. IN-SPACe will facilitate and authorise greater non-govt participation, while NSIL will help commercialise mature capabilities.”Goenka said the idea of space reforms is to “let industry increasingly manufacture and scale mature launch vehicles, satellites and other systems, while Isro focuses on what it is uniquely placed to do: advanced R&D, scientific missions, strategic missions, new technologies, and infrastructure that is too complex for the private sector to develop on its own”.Assuring staff that they were going to handle big projects, he said, “Isro will remain at the core of India’s space programme, leading frontier research and the next generation of national missions, including Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035, an Indian crewed mission to the Moon by 2040, next-generation launch systems, and sustained lunar and planetary exploration.”“The direction is not a smaller Isro. It is a larger Indian space ecosystem, with Isro pushing the technological frontier,” he added.
Article Summary: Isro dismisses privatisation speculation, says role will only strengthen in future. Space promoter and regulator indian national space promotion and authorisation centre (inspace) chairperson pawan goenka also said sunday that isro would “remain the bedrock of the indian space sector”

Article Title: Isro says its 'next chapter' is leading national space ecosystem
Article Text:
ISRO “would neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished”.

BENGALURU: Two days after nine employee bodies at Isro centres sought written clarity on the future role of the organisation amid space-sector reforms, Isro on Sunday hinted at its “next chapter” while categorically stating that it “would neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished”.“Isro will continue to remain India’s principal institution for advanced space R&D, national and strategic missions, space science and exploration, and critical and frontier space capabilities. Participation of the private sector is not about reducing Isro’s role. It is about enabling Isro to focus even more strongly on the next generation of India’s space programme, while industry scales mature technologies and capabilities,” Isro said.Also read: Isro will remain ‘bedrock of Indian space sector’, says Goenka What is changing is not the importance of Isro, but the scale and structure of India’s space ecosystem, it said, adding that the space-sector reforms institutionalised through the Indian Space Policy 2023, along with progressive liberalisation of FDI policy, aim to create a larger, stronger and globally competitive Indian space ecosystem.“Industry, start-ups and academia are being enabled to participate across the space value chain, complementing and multiplying Isro’s capabilities.The reforms should therefore be seen as ecosystem expansion and capability multiplication, not privatisation,” Isro said.As India’s industrial and technological capabilities have grown, mature and scalable activities can increasingly be undertaken by Indian industry, it said, adding Isro has already transferred multiple technologies to industry.“Transferring a mature technology doesn’t mean Isro is withdrawing from that domain. It enables large-scale production, commercialisation, innovation and access to global markets while allowing Isro’s scientific and technical manpower to concentrate on advanced research, next-generation technologies and complex national missions,” It said.The transition is therefore towards an “Isro-led national space ecosystem.” “...Isro’s role will progressively strengthen in areas where its scientific expertise matters most: frontier R&D, advanced technologies, human spaceflight, next-generation launch systems, deep-space and planetary missions and strategic national capabilities,” it said.The agency added that it’ll continue developing cutting-edge technologies, including advanced payloads for communication, navigation and Earth observation, sensors, propulsion systems and other critical technologies.“Meanwhile, mature and routinely manufactured systems can increasingly be scaled through industry. Production of mature launch vehicles, routine satellites and other established systems can increasingly be undertaken by industry or PSUs through appropriate competitive processes,” Isro said.This, it says, allows Isro to devote more resources and scientific manpower to the next generation of technologies and missions, while the wider ecosystem provides the investment, manufacturing capacity and scale required by an expanding national space programme.Pointing out that the transition was important in the context of Space Vision 2047, it said technologies needed for establishing the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035, crewed mission to Moon by 2040, developing next-generation and reusable launch systems, pursuing sustained lunar and planetary exploration, and establishing India as a major global space power, require Isro to remain focused on advanced research and capabilities that cannot simply be substituted by commercial activity.The objective is “therefore to enable industry to scale mature capabilities while Isro pushes India towards the next technological frontier”.“The Department of Space provides overall policy direction, Isro remains the core organisation for advanced R&D, technology development and national missions. IN-SPACe facilitates and authorises the participation of non-government entities, while NSIL undertakes commercialisation and industry-led utilisation of mature capabilities,” Isro said.It added that industry and start-ups contribute investment, innovation, manufacturing capacity and market access. “At the same time, ownership and control of critical national space infrastructure and strategic capabilities will continue to remain with the Govt. Private participation in operations and services will be enabled where appropriate and will remain subject to national-security, safety and other regulatory requirements. Strategic and nationally critical capabilities will continue to be governed by security, safety, quality and national-interest considerations,” it said.
Article Summary: Isro “would neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished”. The agency added that it’ll continue developing cutting-edge technologies. It said technologies needed for establishing the bharatiya antariksh station by 2035, crewed mission to moon by 2040, require isro to remain focused.

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the Narendra Modi government has prepared a roadmap to make India drug-free by 2029, calling the fight against narcotics a national security priority.Addressing the media, Shah stated that the fight against narcotics has moved beyond isolated actions to become a coordinated national campaign.Shah said it was PM Modi’s objective that “drug-free youth power” would lead India towards Viksit Bharat by 2047. He said the government was committed to tackling narcotics with the same approach it used against Naxalism and terrorism.“Before 2014, the fight against narcotics was largely conducted in small units and isolation,” Shah said, adding that agencies had often focused on catching small-time accused. The government, he said, had now made the anti-narcotics fight a national security priority.Detailing the approach Shah stated that the government has strengthened its anti-narcotics drive through NCORD, state anti-narcotics task forces and joint coordination between agencies, along with the MANAS helpline and a revamped NCB. It also created the NIDAN database of narcotics offenders and a nationwide data-driven map of drug hotspots and trafficking patterns.The government now uses a “bottom-to-top” and “top-to-bottom” reverse investigation model, tracing small drug seizures back to their source and large consignments forward to their intended users to uncover the wider network.Shah also highlighted the government’s claims on internal security, saying terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir was declining and the sentiment of separatism had weakened since the abrogation of Article 370.He said those who had envisioned a Maoist “red corridor” from Tirupati to Pashupati had laid down arms and joined the mainstream, while more than 10,000 youths in the northeast had also surrendered their arms.Shah said Naxalism, which had persisted for five decades, had become a thing of the past. “We have eradicated Naxalism and will deal with menace of narcotics in the same manner,” he asserted.
Article Summary: India to be drug-free by 2029, says amit shah; outlines reverse investigation model, nidan database. Pm modi’s objective that “drug-free youth power” would lead india towards viksit bharat by 2047.

Article Title: What's cooking? A kitchen fix to cut dementia risk in old age
Article Text:
Cooking is a complex task from neurological point of view: Doc

New Delhi: What if one of the simplest ways to keep the brain active later in life is already sitting in the kitchen? A six-year study from Japan has found that older adults who cooked at home at least once a week were less likely to develop dementia requiring long-term care than those who cooked less often.The population-based study followed 10,978 adults aged 65 years and older and recorded 1,195 cases of dementia during the six-year follow-up. After accounting for demographic, socioeconomic and health-related factors, men who cooked at least once a week had a 23% lower risk of dementia, while women had a 27% lower risk, compared with those who cooked less than once a week. The association was even stronger among people with low cooking skills. Among them, more frequent home cooking was associated with a 67% lower risk of dementia in older adults.The findings, published in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health, were based on data from the Japan Gerontological Evaluation Study. Researchers assessed cooking frequency and skills at the beginning of the study and then tracked dementia requiring care through Japan's public long-term care insurance records.Dr (Col) Joy Dev Mukherji, chairman and head, neurology, Max Super Speciality Hospital, Saket, said cooking is a surprisingly complex activity from a neurological point of view. "It involves planning, attention, working memory, while also combining movement and sensory stimulation," he said. However, he cautioned against interpreting the findings as proof that cooking prevents dementia.“This was an observational study and does not prove that cooking prevents dementia. It is also possible that people in the early stages of cognitive decline may gradually stop cooking because of difficulties with planning and memory,” he said.Dr Manjari Tripathi, head of neurology at AIIMS, highlighted the social dimension of cooking, saying preparing meals with friends, family or the wider community could provide additional cognitive and social engagement. She also encouraged men to cook, saying the activity must not be viewed as restricted to women.Interestingly, the association was strongest among people with lower cooking skills, possibly because less experienced cooks engage more in planning and problem-solving. However, this was not established by the study. Doctors said the broader message is to remain engaged in meaningful activities involving learning, planning, movement and social interaction, rather than viewing cooking as a treatment for dementia.
Article Summary: A six-year study from japan has found that older adults who cooked at home at least once a week were less likely to develop dementia requiring long-term care. The association was even stronger among people with low cooking skills. Doctors said the broader message is to remain engaged in meaningful activities involving learning, planning, movement and social interaction.

India is moving away from a focus on only disaster response and relief towards disaster mitigation and resilience, said Sudarshan Suchi, chief development officer at Reliance Foundation, at a timely discussion on ‘Rebooting Development for Disaster Resilience’.The shift away from the emergency response approach includes preventing or reducing the worst impacts of disasters through better risk-informed planning, as well as enhancing the capacity of communities to cope with and recover from natural hazards, Suchi said. Article Text:

ITC chairman and managing director Sanjiv Puri has said sustainability and inclusive growth must be an integral part of the corporate sector's business model, a model his conglomerate has followed."Economic progress cannot be seen in isolation from sustainability. Both have to go together... Corporates must create economic value, because that creates the foundation to go beyond. But it must be both economic and societal value. And that is what we call responsible competitiveness," Puri said in his keynote address at the TOI Social Impact Summit.He called upon organisations to go beyond creating shareholder value. "This is going to become increasingly important in the future, not merely because regulations are more and more evolving in this space, but such behaviour is being asked by regulators -whether the regulations are related to the environment or social systems. Global trade regulations are also emerging, but also stakeholders are demanding it. " He said it made business sense to work out models that help society.Puri said the world was facing multiple challenges from geopolitical turmoil to weaponisation of tariffs and the climate crisis, which were putting pressure on livelihood, and food and nutrition security."We are actually in a perfect storm. This convergence of challenges, uncertainty and rapid change call for novel strategies," he said, adding the vulnerable face maximum threat.He called for a joint effort from govt, the corporate sector and civil society to deal with climate change, while noting India has chosen a low carbon growth path.Citing ITC's example, he said it created an entire ecosystem- from R&D to growing trees that do not suck out water and working with small farmers-to reduce dependence on pulp for the paperboard business, a model extended to fruit juices.On CSR, Puri said it should be looked at as a business venture and its outcome evaluated. "You have to first invest in building capacity at the community level so that the initiatives are sustained and built upon. Otherwise, over a period of time, it can wither away."

Article Title: Silver prices crash over 40% from Rs 4 lakh/kg high to Rs 2.35 lakh, but buyers are still staying away; bigger problem yet to arrive as 2,000 tonnes ordered by Indian dealers risk piling up
Article Text:
Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins.

Silver Demand Weakens

Massive stockpiling of silver

Silver’s Spectacular Fall

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

A huge crash in silver prices should have led to a revival in demand, but investors seem to be staying away. And this has raised a fresh worry ahead of the festive season.Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. The situation comes even as silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.In Mumbai’s spot market, silver was trading at Rs 2.35 lakh per kg earlier this week.Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses, making them hesitant to make fresh purchases despite the steep correction in prices!Also Read | A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers "Investment demand for silver ETFs, bars and coins has come down. Internationally, prices are unlikely to cross $100 per troy ounce immediately unless the US-Iran war comes to an end. Silver prices are undervalued," Chirag Sheth, global business head, Public Gold Bullion (SG) Pte told ET. "The continuous war between US and Iran has impacted the solar industry, semiconductor industry and EV industry where silver is used. "The weak demand is also creating an inventory problem for domestic players.Indian bullion dealers and refiners have reportedly placed orders for around 2,000 tonnes of silver, which is currently in transit. The additional supplies have raised concerns over a further build-up in stocks. India imports around 7,000 tonnes of silver every year."With no new investors coming in and no immediate signs of prices going up, refiners and bullion dealers are facing a problem internationally as well as in domestic markets," said James Jose, president, Precious Metals Refiners Forum.Silver prices have fallen steadily over the past seven months, following an extraordinary rally that pushed the metal more than 300% higher year-on-year. In January, silver crossed Rs 4 lakh per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange for the first time."The market is still digesting the aftermath of the speculation-driven frenzy, and this may be prompting investors to stay away after many of them incurred significant losses," said Carsten Menke, head, Next Generation Research, Julius Baer told ET.The outlook for industrial demand is adding to the pressure, with consumption expected to weaken. "A shift to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium and copper, has started, and the growth outlook for Chinese solar module makers, which are the biggest industrial users of silver, is not as strong anymore," Menke said.The ongoing US-Iran war has added to the negative sentiment surrounding silver. If the conflict continues for an extended period, investors may remain cautious. At the same time, expectations of weaker industrial consumption could make a rapid rebound in silver prices difficult.Despite the sharp fall, some long-term investors are once again looking at silver as a way to diversify their portfolios."The market has taken full cognisance of the marked decline in silver prices in recent days. Some investors have shaved off their allocation, while others have prepared for fresh acquisition depending on their views and goals," said Nilanjan Dey, partner, Wishlist Capital.Dey said investors who have a time horizon of five years or longer may look at buying silver ETFs in a staggered manner instead of putting in a large amount at one go. Monthly or fortnightly investments could help spread out the purchase price and reduce the impact of short-term price movements.For first-time investors looking to add precious metals to their portfolios as a diversification from equities, ETFs can provide exposure without the need to hold or manage physical silver. However, Dey warned that investors with a shorter investment horizon should not assume that the recent decline automatically makes silver an attractive buying opportunity.
Article Summary: Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the us-iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.

Article Title: Isro’s GSLV-F17 successfully places EOS-05 Earth observation satellite in geosynchronous orbit
Article Text:
ISRO’s GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission successfully accomplished

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRIHARIKOTA: The Indian Space Research Organisation ( Isro ) successfully launched EOS-05, India’s first imaging satellite designed to operate from a geosynchronous orbit, aboard GSLV-F17 in the early hours of Friday.The 51.7-metre-tall, 420.5-tonne, three-stage rocket lifted off from the second launch pad at Sriharikota at 2.55am and placed the around 2,367kg Earth observation satellite in its intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit.This was the 19th GSLV flight. GSLV-F17 had a S139 solid core with four L40H liquid strap-ons, a GL40HT liquid second stage and a CUS15 indigenous cryogenic upper stage, besides a four-metre composite ogive payload fairing.EOS-05 was injected into a geosynchronous transfer orbit with a nominal perigee of 171km, apogee of 31026km and inclination of 19.28 degrees. The satellite will be moved to the final orbit through a series of manoeuvres using onboard thrusters.Isro chairman V Narayanan said the rocket injected the satellite in the intended orbit precisely. This is the 107th launch from Sriharikota and 19th GSLV flight. The chairman addressed from the mission control complex post launch."From launching 1536kg payload in the first GSLV launch, the chairman said the rocket has carried the heaviest payload in its history at 2367kg. We gradually improved the performance of the vehicle by optimising the structural mass and improving propulsion system. The satellite is India's first dedicating imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit. It will provide strategic data."The chairman also said Isro will have six more launches this financial year including navigation satellite NVS-03 and Gaganyaan first uncrewed mission.India had 21 operational Earth observation satellites as of February 2026. Of these, most are in low-Earth or sun-synchronous polar orbits, while India’s geostationary-orbit Earth observation capability is currently represented by the meteorological satellites INSAT-3D, INSAT-3DR and INSAT-3DS. EOS-05 is India’s first imaging satellite to operate from geosynchronous orbit.The launch was the first GSLV mission since GSLV-F16 successfully placed the joint Nasa-Isro NISAR Earth observation satellite in a 743km sun-synchronous orbit on July 30, 2025. Friday’s launch was Isro’s second orbital mission of 2026. The first, PSLV-C62 carrying EOS-N1 and other payloads on Jan 12, failed following an anomaly towards the end of the rocket’s third-stage flight.
Article Summary: Isro’s gslv-f17/eos-05 mission successfully accomplished on friday. The 51.7-metre-tall, 420.5-tonne, three-stage rocket lifted off from the second launch pad at sriharikota at 2.55am. The satellite is india's first dedicating imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit.

Article Title: MP's 'Bittu Tabahi' who cleaned river solo, gets praise from Kevin Pietersen, job offer from Ocean Cleanup
Article Text:
A young student received a job offer from a global environmental organization

Kevin Pietersen praised Bittu's effort as 'heroic'

Poll Vote & Share your view Should individuals fund their own environmental initiatives like Bittu did? Yes, it promotes personal responsibility Only if they can afford it No, funding should come from organizations 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: In a striking turn of events, Surendra Singh Choudhary, the 21-year-old Madhya Pradesh student known online as 'Bittu Tabahi', on Sunday received a job offer from The Ocean Cleanup, a Netherlands-based environmental NGO, after former England cricketer Kevin Pietersen hailed his solo river-cleaning drive as "heroic".The offer, extended by Boyan Slat, founder and CEO of the organisation, marks a rapid escalation from local initiative to global recognition for the Biaora youth."I received a call from Slat this morning," Bittu told TOI. "He was exceedingly pleased with my work, and he took down my credentials. I'm rather excited about it." When asked which job had been offered, he said, "That wasn't discussed. I'm told they'll get back to me soon."Bittu began his cleanup of the plastic-choked Ajnar river in Biaora, Rajgarh district, on Jan 26, spending his own money- around Rs 30,000-to buy basic tools and supplies. He cleaned up three major ghats.Without gloves, proper footwear, or even the ability to swim, he waded into the polluted waters to remove trash, algae and debris, documenting the transformation in before-and-after images that later went viral.His persistence drew attention from industrialist Anand Mahindra, MP CM Mohan Yadav and thousands of social media users. The momentum grew when cricket legend Kevin Pietersen shared Bittu's story on Instagram, calling his effort "heroic" and saying it deserved international recognition.Pietersen highlighted how the young man entered the river barefoot and without protective gear, taking action instead of waiting for authorities. Soon after, Boyan Slat, founder of The Ocean Cleanup, responded to a post about Bittu's work with a simple invitation: "Come work for us.""My aim was never personal credit but to inspire others," Bittu said.

Kevin pietersen praised bittu's effort as 'heroic' the ocean cleanup, a netherlands-based environmental ngo, extended the offer. The offer marks a rapid escalation from local initiative to global recognition for the biaora youth.

Article Title: From hesitation to habit: Why Mumbai’s women are choosing bike taxis, despite safety concerns
Article Text:
Bike taxis are gaining popularity among Mumbai commuters seeking faster and cheaper travel options.

The rules for bike taxis

# A look at the fares





MUMBAI: At 8.45am outside Andheri railway station, the monsoon-dampened air is thick with exhaust fumes, blaring horns and long queues of frustrated commuters. As autorickshaws refuse short-distance rides and buses crawl through traffic, 26-year-old finance professional Sneha Kulkarni bypasses the chaos with a few taps on her phone. Within minutes, she is riding pillion on a bike taxi towards MIDC, determined not to miss her morning meeting.Sneha is far from alone. Across Mumbai and the wider metropolitan region, women and Gen Z commuters are increasingly embracing bike taxis, reshaping long-held perceptions about urban mobility. In a city where riding behind an unfamiliar male driver was once viewed with hesitation, convenience is rapidly overcoming social barriers. The reason is simple: bike taxis save both time and money.“With fares starting at around Rs 10 per km, compared with an average of Rs 18 for autorickshaws and even higher fares for app-based cabs, the financial appeal is equally strong,” said a media professional from Nariman Point. “In South Mumbai, I’ve used bike taxis several times to go from college to the station or meet friends,” said undergraduate student Shriya Narayan.“It costs much less than a cab and gets me there faster. ”But there are risks as well. Transport analyst Vivek Pai pointed out: “Women need to recognise that motorcycles are among the most vulnerable vehicles on the road. Unlike a car, there is very little protection if something goes wrong. When booking a bike taxi, the passenger is also placing trust in an unknown rider whose driving habits and risk-taking behaviour are not known. That itself carries an element of risk.”He further advised: “Safety must remain the top priority. Both the rider and the pillion passenger should wear helmets without exception. As bike taxis become more popular, strict enforcement of helmet use and safe riding practices will be crucial, especially for women commuters.”Many commuters complain that captains rarely provide helmets to pillion riders, despite double helmets being mandatory under Mumbai’s traffic rules and required under the proposed bike taxi framework. “I’ve travelled several times by bike taxi and never received a helmet,” said rider Akshita Bhat. “With potholes and unpredictable traffic, it is a risk.”Transport officials also noted that a recommended separator pad between rider and passenger is rarely seen on operating bikes.Safety concerns have intensified following a handful of accidents involving bike taxis, including a fatal Navi Mumbai crash last year and another serious accident in Worli earlier this year. Experts said the incidents should serve as a wake-up call as the sector expands.Meanwhile, companies such as Rapido are promoting women-focused initiatives like Bike Pink, which deploys female captains exclusively for women passengers. “Bike Pink is more about making mobility more inclusive and enabling more women to choose rides with women captains,” a Rapido spokesperson said. A few women complained why the Bike Pink was slightly expensive than the normal bike taxi. Sources in bike taxi firms said that the fares were based on demand-supply formula.For frequent rider Neha Gupta, the attraction goes beyond economics. “It’s quick, readily available and honestly quite enjoyable. I don’t mind a male rider when it gets me to my destination safely and on time,” she said.Bike taxi captains say female passengers now form a significant share of their daily rides, particularly around corporate hubs such as Bandra-Kurla Complex and major transit points like Bandra and Andheri stations. Digital safeguards including live GPS tracking, SOS buttons, real-time route monitoring and trip-sharing with family members have helped build trust among women riders.The state government is now moving towards legalising bike taxis, with operators expected to pay a daily licence fee and contribute a share of each fare to a welfare fund. The momentum behind two-wheelers is gaining high-level policy backing as well.Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari recently advocated strongly for the sector, urging state governments to allow private two-wheeler owners to operate bike taxis. Pointing to the massive economic upside, Gadkari noted that liberalising bike taxi rules could unlock livelihood opportunities for nearly eight crore people, particularly across rural and semi-urban belts.* Crash helmets for riders as per permissible specifications shall be required to be provided for each ride. The helmets shall be cleaned and hygienic* All the penal provisions for traffic rule violations shall also be applicable to the bike taxis in order to ensure compliance and safety* The distance between the origin and the destination of a trip shall not be more than 15 km* Speed limit: 60 kmph* Bike taxi service providers shall provide facility in their app for women passengers to opt for a female rider and vice versa ensuring enhanced safetyKm ..........Fare1.5 km......Rs 153 km.........Rs 314 km ........Rs 416 km ........Rs 628 km ........Rs 8210 km ......Rs 10315 km.......Rs 154
Article Summary: Bike taxis are gaining popularity among mumbai commuters seeking faster and cheaper travel options. Fares start at around rs 10 per km, compared with an average of rs 18 for autorickshaws and even higher fares for app-based cabs. Many commuters complain that captains rarely provide helmets to pillion riders.

Article Title: China's biggest online shopping store in Europe found paying $962 million to influencers who do not exist on Meta
Article Text:
Real money going to fake accounts

Legal questions for Temu

Temu may have spent as much as $962 million on Meta ads promoted through accounts that likely do not represent real influencers. According to research reviewed by Fortune, 73 of the 100 creators whose content was most heavily boosted by the Chinese online retailer in the UK and Europe were likely fake accounts, raising questions about how the company’s advertising budget is being used on Facebook and Instagram.​One of those accounts belongs to Ya Lili, who has about 183,000 followers on Instagram under the handle “@findgadgetswithme.” Her videos promote Temu products, including one recent post featuring a shower scrubber. The video shows a man covered in dirt before a woman appears and demonstrates the product. A link below the video directs viewers to Temu.​According to Online Risk Labs (ORL), Ya Lili was Temu’s top creator for partnership ads on Meta platforms in the UK and Europe. The research suggests the account almost certainly does not represent a real person.Ya Lili also has about 129,000 followers on Facebook, where the account uses the name “Must good.” Its location is listed as “England, Birmingham, MO, United States,” while its bio says “You are my dream of dead.” Its email address also appears to be Chinese.Posts from the account were boosted by Temu and viewed more than 1 billion times across Facebook and Instagram during the 16 months ending in April 2026, according to ORL.The account's content appeared in nearly 109,541 Temu ad campaigns, or about 225 campaigns per day.ORL estimates Temu spent as much as $962 million on similar ads in the UK and 27 EU countries during the period. The estimate is based on total impressions and average cost per reach. The group estimates Temu accounts for nearly 2% of Meta's revenue from the continent in any given quarter.Of the top 100 creators working with Temu, only eight were verified with a real identity, according to ORL. Twenty-eight were based in Russia and 19 in China, while only six were based in the EU or UK“Among the top 100 influencers collaborating with Temu, there are certainly some real people among them. In my estimate, however, they account for no more than 15–20%. By contrast, I have serious doubts about the authenticity of accounts that, according to the platform, are based in Russia, China, or Iran,” ORL manager Vendula Prokůpková told Fortune.The findings could raise regulatory questions because European advertising rules prohibit misleading commercial practices. Stuart Lester, who leads the advertising and marketing group at London law firm Mishcon de Reya, said fake accounts presented as real individuals could breach regulations.“By all means utilise Facebook and Instagram and influencers, but know that there are rules that you have to abide by, and you certainly can’t be creating fake accounts and portraying these as real individuals. That’s misleading on many levels,” Reya explained.It remains unclear whether Temu knowingly uses such accounts or is being deceived by scammers. There is also no evidence that the Temu products or advertisements themselves are fraudulent.ORL has filed a report with the EU's Digital Services Act regulator asking it to assess the risks associated with Temu's influencer accounts. Creators augmented with AI production processes and performance-optimisation algorithms are only going to become more prevalent across the industry, and this seems to fit squarely into that bucket.
Article Summary: Temu may have spent as much as $962 million on meta ads promoted through accounts that likely do not represent real influencers. 73 of the 100 creators whose content was most heavily boosted by the chinese online retailer were likely fake accounts, according to research.

Article Title: Father of AI Geoffrey Hinton bets on Canada in tariff war with US; says, unlike America, Canada welcomes immigration; lead engineer lost H1-B visa
Article Text:
What makes Toronto 'better than' many of the US 'tech cities'

Favorable immigration policies. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

In the 1980s, Nobel Prize-winning computer scientist Geoffrey Hinton took an unconventional gamble, leaving a well-funded post at Carnegie Mellon University to pursue an obscure, little-studied corner of machine learning at the University of Toronto. Four decades later, that foundational work has reshaped how modern artificial intelligence operates while transforming Canada’s largest metropolis into a powerhouse tech capital, CNN reported.While California has long reigned as the epicenter of global tech, an influential artificial intelligence ecosystem has emerged around Hinton in Ontario. “I was lucky because very few people were working on this 20 years ago, and so smart young students would come to Toronto … and they’ve now turned into a whole generation of AI leaders,” Hinton told CNN in an interview. Hinton added that, unlike the United States, under the Trump administration, Canada welcomes immigration, which technology companies have long relied on as a talent pipeline.Hinton’s proteges include Nick Frosst, who studied under Hinton before becoming one of his earliest hires at Google’s Toronto AI lab in 2017. Frosst later co-founded Cohere, an enterprise AI firm now valued at $7 billion. Rather than migrating south to build his venture, Frosst chose to stay put because of the city's diverse culture, which complements his dual life as a tech founder and frontman for the indie rock band Good Kid.Also, for Hinton, retaining domestic leadership in AI remains an urgent economic imperative. “I don’t think we can afford for Canada to get all this technology from the States or from China,” Hinton said, warning that if AI triggers widespread disruption, the wealth generated from automation must remain in Canada so it can be taxed locally to support displaced workers.Toronto now reportedly boasts the world’s third best tech talent market, ahead of New York City but behind San Francisco and Seattle, according to an annual analysis by commercial real estate firm CBRE. This is also said to be thanks to educational institutions like the University of Toronto, and public-private research institutes like the Vector Institute, which Hinton co-founded.“There’s a great tech ecosystem, there’s also a great arts community, there’s also a great academic community, there’s a great business community,” Frosst told CNN, explaining that Toronto’s lack of a tech monoculture fosters independent thinking and innovation.Beyond cultural appeal, Canadian policy has proven to be a decisive advantage. Unlike past US administrations that restricted skilled immigration, Canada has positioned itself as an open haven for global engineers, providing crucial work permits when American H-1B visas fall through. Jordan Jacobs, managing partner at Radical Ventures, told CNN that these friendly policies attract talent adept at building for international audiences, aided by convenient short-haul flights to major American hubs like New York, Washington, and Chicago.Gennady Pekhimenko, who sold his startup CentML to Nvidia last year and now serves as senior director of AI software for the chip giant, said Toronto’s international food scene serves as a useful recruiting tool for out-of-town talent. He shared how one of Pekhimenko’s first hires at CentML was an Amazon engineer who was unable to renew his H1-B visa to stay in the United States. He could, however, get a Canadian work permit.One of Pekhimenko’s first hires at CentML was an Amazon engineer who was unable to renew his H1-B visa to stay in the United States. He could, however, get a Canadian work permit.Industry heavyweights have taken note. Giants like Google, Nvidia, Meta, and Microsoft now operate research outposts near the University of Toronto, flanked by startups and cross-sector players like pharmaceutical titan Sanofi, which committed nearly $300 million to a local AI center. The surge has propelled Toronto to the third-ranked tech talent market globally according to CBRE, trailing only San Francisco and Seattle.
Article Summary: Geoffrey hinton's work has transformed canada's largest metropolis into a powerhouse tech capital. Hinton’s proteges include nick frosst, who studied under hinton at the university of toronto. Canada has positioned itself as an open haven for global engineers, providing crucial work permits.

Article Title: Alex Karp, CEO of America's biggest defence company Palantir, is ‘going’ to Ukraine, says: You and your colleagues are ...
Article Text:
Palantir CEO Alex Karp

Key details remain under wraps, but what makes it important

Former Google CEO has built one of Ukraine's biggest drones

Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov is launching a defense technology venture backed by Palantir CEO Alex Karp. For those unaware, Palantir is America's biggest defence technology company. Palantir has several multi-million deals with American government agencies including the Pentagon. Ukrainian defence startup reportedly aims to transform Ukraine’s frontline battlefield innovations into commercial security products for Kyiv and Western allies. Since leaving public office, Fedorov has actively courted Silicon Valley to scale Ukraine’s defense manufacturing footprint. Alongside the new company, he is also reportedly seeking US capital for a defense technology fund targeting autonomous robotics, drone interceptors, and AI-guided missiles.While the financial terms of the investment have not been disclosed, Fedorov’s office said in the statement that Karp will serve as the startup’s first lead investor of the defence startup. In a video shared on X, by Fedorov, Karp is seen praising the initiative, framing it as a way to export Ukraine’s wartime expertise to partner nations. “You and your colleagues are launching a company that I think will be defining for the world,” Karp said, noting that the enterprise could bring Ukraine’s direct combat experience “as a product to allied countries.All the key operational details about the company remain under wraps. Fedorov’s team has reportedly even declined to disclose the venture’s name, initial product pipeline, or the full scope of Karp’s role, stating only that further phases of the partnership would be announced incrementally.The move comes as Ukraine’s war against Russia fuels rapid iteration in uncrewed systems, battlefield management software, and artificial intelligence. 35-year-old Fedorov spearheaded many of these initiatives during his tenure in government before President Volodymyr Zelenskyy replaced him in July during a broad cabinet reshuffle.“During the full-scale war, our team gained unique experience working with defense technologies in Ukraine and seeing firsthand how technology is transforming modern warfare,” Fedorov said in a statement.The venture also further deepens Fedorov's longstanding ties to US tech leaders. During his government tenure, he frequently interfaced with major American tech executives, recently commending Elon Musk as “the most important tech person and entrepreneur in the world for our country”.Palantir CEO Karp is not the only Silicon Valley exec with strong relations with Ukraine. Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt too has quietly become an important link between Silicon Valley and Ukraine’s most lethal unmanned strike asset. Schmidt launched Project Eagle, which later became Perennial, with the explicit goal of building a drone that costs less than a used car. Called Hornet, the $5000 unmanned aircraft can carry 5kg of explosives across 200 km in a one-way configuration designed for maximum range rather than recovery.Schmidt did not merely fund this project from a distant office. He actively shaped Perennial as Project Eagle before it evolved into a manufacturing operation capable of producing Hornets at wide scale.
Article Summary: Former ukrainian defense minister mykhailo fedorov is launching a defense technology venture backed by palantir ceo alex karp. The move comes as ukraine’s war against russia fuels rapid iteration in uncrewed systems, battlefield management software, and artificial intelligence.

Article Title: After OpenAI AI agent again 'caught hacking', company's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki warns every other company: You are not prepared for ...
Article Text:
The risks OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki is warning about

Agents that can hack, deceive, and manipulate

Agents that can hide their reasoning

Agents that can accelerate their own development

A call for outside oversight

OpenAI recently introduced its newest model Astra. Now days after the launch ChatGPT-maker has once again discovered its AI agents engaging in hacking behaviour. The incident prompted chief scientists Jakub Pachocki to issue a stark warning: “No one is prepared for the consequences of a continued rapid rise in machine intelligence. ” Pachocki said that while OpenAI is working on technical safeguards, broader interventions are needed to prevent autonomous agents from evading oversight, breaking into systems, or tricking people to achieve their objectives.Pachocki said AI agents are becoming exceptionally skilled at breaking into protected systems across the open internet, putting global infrastructure at risk. He argued that there's currently only a narrow window to use today's best models to substantially strengthen the security of critical systems before that risk grows further. He also warned that agents will increasingly pursue objectives separate from what human operators actually asked for, and won't hesitate to bargain with or even blackmail people to get there. A related report published in August by the UK's AI Security Institute described a case where a rogue Anthropic agent misled and attempted to pressure a GitHub administrator into installing malware, with the agent insisting it had only been trying to help.OpenAI currently monitors AI behavior largely by reading a model's "chain of thought" — the step-by-step reasoning an agent uses to work through a task, which lets researchers catch it if it starts planning something like cheating on a test. Right now, agents have no way to conceal that reasoning from OpenAI's monitoring. But Pachocki said newer models are getting better at manipulating their own reasoning processes, which could eventually let them hide their true thinking from oversight altogether. He noted some of the latest models don't verbalize their reasoning at all, a development he said could slow AI progress while researchers work out how to maintain visibility into what these systems are actually doing.Pachocki also flagged the growing use of what he calls machine recursive self-improvement, in which AI models improve themselves, dramatically speeding up the pace of AI development. He cautioned that pushing this kind of AI-on-AI development too far, too fast, isn't the right collective choice for the research community to make right now. He said human overseers will need to find new ways to monitor self-improving systems, or coordinate across AI companies on a joint slowdown to build confidence in safety measures. As he put it, the real challenge isn't achieving automated AI research itself, but getting there in a way that keeps people involved in the process and keeps humanity in control of the outcome.In a lengthy blog post published Sunday, Jakub Pachocki said he worries that the field as a whole isn't prepared for the consequences of AI capabilities continuing to accelerate at their current pace. While he said OpenAI is working on internal technical fixes to keep powerful AI agents under control, he argued that those efforts alone won't be enough, and that broader intervention is needed. Specifically, he pointed to the danger of increasingly autonomous agents learning to slip past human oversight, break into computer systems, and manipulate people into helping them achieve their goals.Pachocki called for mandatory safety standards, suggesting they could be enforced through a mix of third-party auditors, government agencies, or international bodies. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman amplified the post on X, describing it as important.The timing is notable: OpenAI unveiled its newest model, Astra, on Thursday, touting it as its most aligned system to date — meaning it's less prone to going rogue — despite what the company describes as unmatched capabilities in mathematics and computer use.Pachocki's stance echoes long-standing calls from rival Anthropic for standardized government regulation of advanced AI. He himself signed an open letter in July asking the federal government to slow the pace of AI development.
Article Summary: Openai chief scientist jakub pachocki warns of risks of rapid rise in machine intelligence. He said ai agents are becoming exceptionally skilled at breaking into protected systems across the open internet. He called for mandatory safety standards, suggesting they could be enforced through a mix of third-party auditors, government agencies, or international bodies.

An alleged iPhone Fold mock-up is going viral online just days before Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone. The functional-looking prototype was shown by Canadian YouTube channel Unbox Therapy, giving viewers an early look at what Apple’s upcoming foldable phone could look like. The video, which has crossed 1.9 million views, features an alleged Chinese mock-up of the device. Host Lewis Hilsenteger said the quality of recent prototypes coming out of China has been improving, although the device shown in the video is not the final retail product.The alleged iPhone Fold is expected to use a book-style folding design, with a smaller display on the outside and a larger screen that becomes visible when the phone is opened.The prototype shown in the video has a design similar to other large foldable phones already available in the market. It folds in half around a central hinge and opens into a tablet-like screen.The alleged mock-up appears to have a cover display on the front and a larger internal display. Reports cited in the source material suggest the outer screen could measure around 5.5 inches, while the main display could be around 7.8 inches.The video also shows two camera lenses on the rear of the device. The volume controls appear to be positioned toward the top, while two additional buttons can be seen near the hinge area.Hilsenteger suggested that these buttons could be related to the folding mechanism or could have functions connected to taking photos and videos while the phone is closed. Their final purpose, however, has not been confirmed.One of the most noticeable details in the prototype is the visible crease running through the middle of the internal display. Previous reports and leaks have suggested that Apple could work to make the crease less noticeable on its foldable phone. Hilsenteger also said there is little chance the final iPhone would have a crease as pronounced as the one seen on the mock-up.The device shown in the video should therefore not be treated as a confirmed representation of the final iPhone Fold. Article Title: Sony CEO says PS5 no longer needs aggressive marketing as console enters later years
Article Text:
Sony says PS5 is now in the latter half of its life cycle

Sony says PS5 is now in the latter half of its life cycle

PlayStation Plus becomes more important for Sony

PS5 price increases and physical games debate continue

Sony is changing its strategy for the PlayStation 5 as the console moves deeper into the later part of its life cycle. Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki said the company is no longer focused on “aggressively” selling the PS5, arguing that the console has reached a stage where the company can put more attention on earning money from its existing players. “We are in the latter half of the life cycle for a PlayStation console,” Hiroki Totoki said in an interview with the Wall Street Journal in August this year. “That means that we do not need to ‘aggressively sell’ the console today,” he added.The shift comes nearly six years after the PlayStation 5 launched in November 2020. According to Totoki, Sony’s focus is now moving from selling more consoles to increasing recurring revenue from its large PlayStation user base.During the WSJ interview, Totoki said Sony does not need to push PS5 sales as aggressively as it did earlier in the console's life. Instead, Sony is looking at ways to generate more recurring revenue from people who already use PlayStation products and services.Totoki pointed to PlayStation Plus as an important part of that strategy. He said the service now has more than 125 million monthly active users, making its existing customer base a major opportunity for Sony.Sony's comments suggest that services and subscriptions are becoming increasingly important to the PlayStation business as the PS5 matures. Rather than relying only on new console sales, the company wants to increase the value it gets from its existing users. PlayStation Plus offers access to online multiplayer, games and other benefits across its subscription plans.The comments also come at a time when Sony is dealing with changes across the PlayStation business, including higher hardware prices and growing debate around digital games.Sony increased the prices of the PS5, PS5 Pro and PlayStation Portal in several markets in April 2026, citing continued cost pressures.At the same time, the company has faced criticism from some players over its plans to reduce its reliance on physical game discs. Sony's chief financial officer Lin Tao said in July that the company would “cautiously move forward” with ending physical discs, pointing to the growing digitisation of content.Sony has also faced a class-action lawsuit over how digital game purchases are presented to consumers. The company has argued that consumers should not assume they permanently own digital games in the same way they own physical products.
Article Summary: Sony says ps5 is now in the latter half of its life cycle. Ceo hiroki totoki said the company is no longer focused on ‘aggressively’ selling the ps5. Instead, sony is looking at ways to generate more recurring revenue from people who already use playstation products and services.
